install_tell: VS Code / JetBrains extension; `cn` CLI (npm install -g @continuedev/cli)
misconfig_patterns: Continue is a CLIENT — no first-party self-hosted server exists. The operator-side surface to assess is the UPSTREAM LLM gateway that Continue is pointed at (Ollama 11434, LiteLLM 4000, vLLM 8000, TGI 80/3000/8080).

Local JSON-RPC channel between IDE webview and Continue core is bound to localhost; if ever observed reachable across the network that mis-binding is itself the finding (CVE-2026-8770 lsTool path traversal becomes remotely exploitable in that misconfig).
config.yaml committed to public repos can leak operator's upstream-gateway URL + apiKey — github-code-search class, not a network-probe class.
Continue Hub (hub.continue.dev / Mission Control) is SaaS-only; there is no self-hosted Hub to scan.

active_probe.false_positive_check: No first-party server fingerprint exists because no first-party server is shipped. Any 'Continue' string seen in a banner is operator-side (TLS cert CN, CORS allow-list on a reverse-proxied upstream gateway) and attributes to the upstream platform, not to Continue.

shodan_dorks.notes: No Continue-server Shodan dork is meaningful. Route population questions to upstream platforms: ollama, litellm, vllm, tgi (see their tome entries).

deployment_tells: Operator stacks following the canonical Continue self-host guide run Ollama (11434) -> LiteLLM (4000) -> nginx (443/80), with only nginx public.
TLS cert CN containing continue.dev or hub.continue.dev on a reverse-proxied LLM gateway is a weak operator-attribution signal (rare; operators usually use their own domain).
CI-mode deployment runs `cn` headless inside a GitHub Action; no network listener.
config.yaml leaking from a public repo with embedded gateway apiKey is the realistic Continue-related finding pattern.
pivot_paths: Identify operator stack -> shadow-sweep 11434 (Ollama), 4000 (LiteLLM), 8000 (vLLM), 8080 (TGI) on same IP/ASN.
github code search `filename:config.yaml continuedev` -> harvest exposed upstream-gateway URLs + apiKeys (separate engagement scope required).
If a Continue JSON-RPC channel is ever observed on a non-loopback interface, treat as a chained misconfiguration finding (CVE-2026-8770 lsTool path traversal becomes remotely reachable).
vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-8770 — Continue (continuedev/continue) <=1.2.22: path traversal in core/tools/implementations/lsTool.ts via unvalidated dirPath over local JSON-RPC. Attack vector: LOCAL. No vendor advisory at publication; vendor non-responsive.

GitHub issue #9025 — community-reported privacy complaint: extension allegedly transmits code/telemetry to api.github.com/copilot_internal/user and us.i.posthog.com despite local-only configuration. Not a CVE.

scope_verdict.verdict: CLI/extension-only — out of scope for Continue-branded Shodan-population probing. The platform's attack surface lives on its UPSTREAM gateways (Ollama, LiteLLM, vLLM, TGI), which are in scope under their own tome entries. The CLI-only verdict IS the finding for this platform (Insight #21 / agno-survey pattern).
scope_verdict.exposed_surface_summary: Local JSON-RPC channel (localhost only). No HTTP daemon. No --port flag in CLI. No on-prem Hub. Mission Control is SaaS-only.

description: Open-source AI coding assistant: VS Code/JetBrains extension + `cn` CLI. Repo is read-only as of 2026-06; product repositioned to CI-quality-checks ('Source-controlled AI checks, enforceable in CI. Powered by the open-source Continue CLI'). Hub (hub.continue.dev) is SaaS-only; Mission Control is the managed cloud config plane.

sources.note: Architecture docs; no server component documented
cn CLI has interactive + headless modes only; no --port / --listen / server mode
Hub described as managed cloud; no self-host option mentioned
Self-hosting guide is about the UPSTREAM model gateway (Ollama/vLLM/TGI), not Continue
Core uses message-passing IDE<->core, no network HTTP server documented
CVE-2026-8770 lsTool path traversal, local attack vector
Canonical self-host stack: Ollama 11434 -> LiteLLM 4000 -> nginx
